goal: Make `kitcode mini` open as the smallest practical always-on-top micro chip instead of the current large mini dashboard.

in: Replace the `/mini` HTML/CSS layout with a compact micro chip focused on break progress percent and status.
Resize the Electron BrowserWindow from the current large fixed mini window to an approximately 160x64 chip, not exceeding 180x80 by default.
Keep the chip always-on-top, frameless, movable, and draggable.
Keep the close control available in the micro layout without interfering with dragging.
Keep live updates using the existing `/api/summary` initial fetch and `/api/events` summary stream.
Show concise states for READY, LIVE, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting/error behavior.
Use the existing reward summary and milestone progress logic; do not change tracker, ledger, reward, or API behavior.
Allow the body of the chip to open the dashboard or another clear detail view while preserving the close button.
out: No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json`.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, or equals counting.
No new backend or campaign claim flow.
No redesign of the full React dashboard.
No new CLI commands or command options unless implementation proves a tiny flag is unavoidable.
No expansion mode for the first version.

acceptance_criteria.summary: Electron mini window defaults to an approximately 160x64 chip and does not exceed 180x80.
`/mini` no longer renders the large ring, metric tiles, long status message, or `Mini.tsx` header.
The chip shows a progress percent plus a concise status label for LIVE, READY, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting/error states.
When any local reward tier has `status === "ready"`, the chip prioritizes the READY state visually and textually.
The chip remains draggable, the close button works, and clicking the chip body opens a clear detail destination without triggering close.
Implementation continues using existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data and does not alter local API or reward contracts.
At the chosen chip size, all labels fit without scrollbars, clipping, or incoherent overlap.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so existing command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Add or perform a focused smoke check that `/mini` HTML contains the micro chip controls and no longer contains the removed large layout elements.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode mini` locally, then verify chip size, drag, close, click behavior, and READY/LIVE/IDLE/OFFLINE text at runtime.

risks.summary: The current Electron window hard-locks minimum and maximum size to 340x430, so both BrowserWindow sizing and HTML body dimensions must change together.
risks.mitigation: Update `mini-electron.mjs` dimensions and remove/replace `mini-window.mjs` body min-width/min-height values in the same implementation.

risks.summary: A frameless draggable chip can conflict with clickable controls and dashboard-open behavior.
risks.mitigation: Use `-webkit-app-region: drag` on the shell and `no-drag` on close/click targets; keep click target behavior simple.

risks.summary: Removing time and equals details may feel sparse to users expecting the current mini dashboard.
risks.mitigation: Use the chip as a glance surface and make clicking it open the full dashboard/detail experience.

risks.summary: When Electron is unavailable, `/mini` opens in a normal browser tab where the chip layout should still look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Center the chip in larger browser viewports while preserving the micro dimensions for Electron.

implementation_handoff.summary: Transform the mini window from a large dashboard card into a micro always-on-top status chip.
suggested_sequence: Update Electron dimensions, min/max size, and placement margin for the micro chip.
Replace mini HTML/CSS with a tiny chip layout that uses system fonts, stable dimensions, no scroll, and compact status styling.
Keep or adapt existing progress calculation and EventSource update code while removing unused time/equals/message node updates.
Add chip body click behavior that opens a detail destination, while the close button remains separate.
Run syntax/build checks and perform a manual visual check of size, drag, close, click, and live state updates.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs currently sets width 340, height 430, minWidth 300, minHeight 360, and locks minimum/maximum size.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-window.mjs currently sets body min-width 320 and min-height 390 and renders a large progress ring, time/equal metric tiles, and a long message.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs already serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, and `/api/events`; no API expansion is needed.
notes: Use existing reward summary fields and ready tier detection.
Do not change persisted state or reward math.
Prefer concise labels over long copy because the selected target is the Micro 160x64 direction.

goal: Redesign `kitcode mini` from the current tiny 160x64 chip into a more polished fixed-size mini panel that is draggable, not resizable, and opens near the bottom-right of the desktop viewport without sitting too deep on the screen.

in: Resize the Electron BrowserWindow from the current 160x64 micro chip to a compact but readable mini panel, targeting approximately 300-320px wide and 136-156px tall.
Place the mini window at the bottom-right of the primary display work area by default, with enough right and bottom margin to avoid feeling clipped or too deep near the dock/taskbar.
Keep the mini window frameless, always-on-top, movable, draggable, and non-resizable.
Keep the close control available and ensure it does not conflict with window dragging.
Replace the micro chip HTML/CSS with a polished mini panel that clearly shows KitCode identity, progress percent, status, and a compact progress indicator.
Keep concise visual states for READY, LIVE, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting/error behavior.
Keep live updates using the existing `/api/summary` initial fetch and `/api/events` summary stream.
Use existing reward summary and milestone progress logic; do not change tracker, ledger, reward, local state, or API behavior.
Preserve body click behavior that opens the dashboard/detail destination while keeping close separate.
out: No user resizing, resize handles, or expanded layout mode in this version.
No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json`.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, equals counting, or milestone contracts.
No new backend or campaign claim flow.
No redesign of the full React dashboard.
No new CLI commands or command options unless implementation proves a tiny flag is unavoidable.

acceptance_criteria.summary: Electron mini window defaults to a fixed compact panel around 300-320px wide and 136-156px tall, large enough to look intentional and readable.

The window opens near the bottom-right of the primary display work area with approximately 24-32px right margin and 64-88px bottom margin, instead of opening at the top-right or too close to the bottom edge.
The window remains draggable and movable but cannot be resized by the user; min and max dimensions match the selected panel size.
`/mini` renders a polished mini panel rather than the current 160x64 micro chip, with stable dimensions, KitCode identity, progress percent, status label, and a compact progress indicator.
When any local reward tier has `status === "ready"`, the panel prioritizes READY state visually and textually over LIVE or IDLE.
The panel shell remains draggable, the close button works without triggering drag or dashboard open, and clicking the main panel body opens the existing dashboard/detail destination.
At the selected fixed panel size, all labels, controls, and progress elements fit without scrollbars, clipping, layout shift, or incoherent overlap.
Implementation continues using existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data and does not alter local API, reward, ledger, tracker, or persistence contracts.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so existing command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Run syntax checks for the mini source files after changing the Electron placement and `/mini` HTML renderer.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode mini` locally, then verify bottom-right placement, fixed size, drag behavior, close behavior, dashboard-open click behavior, and READY/LIVE/IDLE/OFFLINE presentation.

risks.summary: The existing implemented active plan intentionally made the mini window a 160x64 micro chip, so this requirement reverses that UX decision.
risks.mitigation: Treat `comfortable-mini-window` as the newer product direction and update both Electron dimensions and `/mini` body dimensions together.

risks.summary: Bottom-right placement depends on the primary display work area and can feel different across macOS dock positions, Windows taskbars, and multi-monitor setups.
risks.mitigation: Use `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea` and explicit bottom/right margins; keep the first implementation focused on primary display behavior.

risks.summary: A frameless draggable window can conflict with close and dashboard-open click targets.
risks.mitigation: Use `-webkit-app-region: drag` on passive shell/header areas and `-webkit-app-region: no-drag` on close and clickable content.

risks.summary: Adding more visual information than the micro chip can make the mini panel feel busy if the height stays too small.
risks.mitigation: Limit the panel to identity, status, percent, one compact progress bar, and one short hint line; defer metrics tiles and expanded details.

risks.summary: When Electron is unavailable, `/mini` may open in a normal browser tab where fixed panel dimensions should still look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Center the fixed mini panel in larger browser viewports while preserving Electron-sized dimensions.

implementation_handoff.summary: Transform the mini window from an overly small micro chip into a fixed-size, polished bottom-right mini panel while preserving existing local API and reward behavior.
suggested_sequence: Update Electron width and height to the selected compact panel size, keep `resizable: false`, and lock min/max size to those dimensions.
Move default placement from top-right to bottom-right using `workArea.y + workArea.height - height - bottomMargin`, with a larger bottom margin than right margin.
Replace the current chip CSS/HTML with a mini panel layout that uses stable fixed dimensions, no scroll, concise typography, a status pill, and a progress bar.
Keep the existing `getBreakProgress`, ready-tier detection, `/api/summary` fetch, and `/api/events` EventSource update path.
Apply drag/no-drag regions so passive shell/header areas move the window and interactive close/open controls remain clickable.
Run syntax/build checks and perform a manual visual check on desktop.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs currently sets width 160, height 64, minWidth 160, minHeight 64, and locks minimum/maximum size to the chip dimensions.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs currently sets `y` to `workArea.y + margin`, which places the mini window near the top-right rather than bottom-right.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-window.mjs currently sets body min-width 160 and min-height 64 and renders a tiny chip with percent, status, hint, close, and grip.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs already serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, and `/api/events`; no API expansion is needed.
notes: Use existing reward summary fields and ready tier detection.
Do not change persisted state, tracker behavior, reward math, or API contracts.
Prefer a readable mini panel over a large dashboard card; do not restore metric tiles unless the selected size can support them without clutter.
Recommended initial dimensions are 320x148 with right margin 28 and bottom margin 72.

goal: Add `kitcode terminal` as a separate Electron terminal-style window that opens centered, can be dragged and resized freely, and provides a safe KitCode-only fake shell with English Vim-inspired UI.

in: Add a public `kitcode terminal` CLI command.
Make `kitcode terminal` check the local tracker before opening, using the same unavailable-tracker behavior as `dashboard` and `mini`.
Open a separate Electron BrowserWindow centered on the primary display work area by default.
Make the terminal window movable, draggable, and user-resizable with sensible minimum dimensions, similar to a native desktop terminal.
Serve a local terminal HTML view from the tracker, expected as `GET /terminal`.
Render an English-only terminal UI with a large Vim-inspired title treatment, such as `KITCODE TERMINAL`, a Vim-style status/tab line, command output history, and a focused prompt.
Implement a safe KitCode-only command engine for `help`, `status`, `summary`, `rewards`, `dashboard`, `mini`, and `clear`.
Use existing local summary and reward data for status, summary, and rewards output; do not add new persistence.
Support terminal basics: Enter submits, Up/Down navigates command history, `clear` clears output, and unknown commands return a helpful safe-shell message.
Open external dashboard/detail destinations through Electron-safe external opening behavior rather than arbitrary shell execution.
out: No passthrough to the user's real shell, filesystem commands, `child_process` execution from terminal input, or arbitrary command execution.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, equals counting, or local tracker behavior.
No changes to local state persistence under `~/.kitcode/state.json` or tracker metadata under `~/.kitcode/tracker.json`.
No campaign backend, login, claim flow, or remote telemetry.
No redesign of the React dashboard, setup gateway, admin view, or current `kitcode mini` panel.
No dashboard overlay version in the first implementation.

acceptance_criteria.summary: `kitcode terminal` is documented in CLI help, participates in command dispatch, and exits nonzero with the existing tracker-unavailable message when the local tracker is not running.
The command opens a separate Electron window centered in the primary display work area, with `resizable: true`, `movable: true`, and sensible minimum dimensions.
The local tracker serves a terminal HTML view, expected at `GET /terminal`, without changing existing `/mini`, `/api/summary`, `/api/events`, or reward endpoints.
The terminal UI uses English-only copy, displays a large Vim-inspired title such as `KITCODE TERMINAL`, and includes a terminal-style prompt and status/tab line.
The input accepts only safe KitCode terminal commands: `help`, `status`, `summary`, `rewards`, `dashboard`, `mini`, and `clear`; unknown commands do not execute anything and suggest `help`.
The terminal keeps input focused, Enter submits commands, Up/Down navigates command history, and `clear` clears the visible output history.
`status`, `summary`, and `rewards` render from existing local summary and reward contract fields without changing tracker, reward, local state, or API response shapes.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so command, reward, snapshot, ledger, and syntax checks still pass.
Extend CLI command checks so help includes `terminal` and `kitcode terminal` fails with the tracker-unavailable message when no tracker is running.
Add or perform a focused smoke check that the terminal HTML includes the large title, prompt, supported command labels, and no real-shell execution hooks.
Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode terminal`, then verify centered opening, drag, resize, prompt focus, command history, safe command outputs, dashboard open, and no arbitrary shell execution.

risks.summary: A realistic terminal UI may make users expect real shell execution.
risks.mitigation: Keep `help`, unknown-command copy, and supported command outputs explicit that this is a KitCode terminal, not a system shell; never execute arbitrary input.

risks.summary: Frameless custom chrome can make native-feeling resize and drag behavior fragile.
risks.mitigation: Prefer a normal resizable Electron window or carefully limit draggable custom regions; keep minimum dimensions stable and test resize manually.

risks.summary: Adding a public CLI command and `GET /terminal` expands both CLI and local HTTP surface area.
risks.mitigation: Update CLI help, docs, command checks, local HTTP contract notes, and route smoke coverage together.

risks.summary: If Electron is unavailable and the terminal view opens in a browser tab, the layout still needs to look intentional.
risks.mitigation: Make `/terminal` responsive within browser dimensions while keeping the Electron default centered and terminal-like.

risks.summary: A resizable terminal can be shrunk enough to cause title, prompt, or output overlap.
risks.mitigation: Set minimum BrowserWindow dimensions and CSS min sizes that keep the title, status line, and prompt readable.

implementation_handoff.summary: Introduce a safe terminal-style KitCode surface as a separate resizable Electron window launched by `kitcode terminal`.
suggested_sequence: Add terminal URL/open helpers and a `terminal` command branch in `packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs`, mirroring the server check behavior used by `mini`.
Create a terminal Electron entry that opens `http://host:port/terminal`, centers the BrowserWindow in `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea`, and allows resize/move with minimum dimensions.
Create a terminal HTML renderer and serve it from `GET /terminal` in `packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs`.
Implement the browser-side safe command engine using only local API fetches/window actions for supported KitCode commands.
Style the route as an English Vim-inspired terminal with a large `KITCODE TERMINAL` title, status/tab line, output history, and prompt.
Update README/help/contracts/checks for the new command and route.
Run CLI build/checks and perform the manual Electron terminal verification.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently lists `dashboard` and `mini` in help and command dispatch, but no `terminal` command exists.
packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently uses `isServerRunning` and `printTrackerNotRunning` for `dashboard` and `mini`, which should be reused for `terminal`.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs currently serves `/mini`, `/api/summary`, `/api/events`, `/api/projects`, and reward redemption, but no `/terminal` route.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs shows the existing Electron pattern for loading a local tracker URL into a BrowserWindow.
apps/web/src/components/header.tsx and apps/web/src/index.css show the existing terminal/Vim visual language that the terminal view should echo without redesigning the dashboard.
notes: The requested title treatment should be large like a real terminal/Vim surface, not a small modal heading.
Keep command execution local and safe; terminal input must never invoke the user's real shell.
The first implementation should be Electron-only for the launch surface; a dashboard overlay can wait.
